_doc: DSH6 completeness-gate allowlist (Phase 0b). Consumed by
`dsh6-collapse-detector.cjs --gate`: EVERY detector group — collapse AND
class-absent, by-type AND scalar — must have its key here or the gate
fails. This converts the old non-gating class-absent bucket (the blind
spot that let Power of the Depths' +Range drop stay CI-green for two
months) into an enumerated, frozen exception set: a NEW whole-class drop
now fails CI and can only ship via a reviewed addition to this file,
with a reason. Keys: by-type = 'effectType|subType|sign', scalar =
'effectType|sign' (sign '' when unsigned), discriminator =
'kind|effectType' (kind = 'twin-unenhanced' | 'self-penalty').
Reasons distinguish 'by design' (converter documentedly drops it on
purpose) from 'known gap' (real modeling gap, tracked, not yet built).
ALL SIX BUCKETS ARE EMPTY as of 2026-09-26, and that is the correct state, not an
un-filled file. They held 25 allowances until then -- 1 byTypeCollapse, 15 classAbsent,
1 discriminatorCollapse, 2 discriminatorClassAbsent, 6 scalarClassAbsent -- and every
one had gone stale: the detector observes ZERO groups in all six categories, over 5,899
by-type and 1,231 scalar atoms across 3,359/3,359 powers checked, so `GATE PASS -- every
group is enumerated` was true because it enumerated nothing.
Why they went stale is the converter getting BETTER, which was measured rather than
assumed. Eleven of the 25 were Genetic Corruption (Stalker Bio Armor), allowed on the
ground that its `kRestedAdaptation Source.Mode?` stance-gated +Res and +Regen were
'wholly dropped from base output'. Its shard at
pipeline/homecoming/powersets/stalker/secondary/bio-armor.json now carries 29 atoms
including Resistance across all eight damage types, Regeneration, and the kRestedAdaptation
gate string itself. The drop the allowance excused does not happen any more.
Neither this file nor dsh6-collapse-worklist.json has changed since d4eaf49ae, and the
committed worklist has been all-zero for that whole time -- so these allowances never
described THIS repo's output at all. Like the two `.test.ts` guards the export manifests
still cite and the CI command removed in 158de4710, they arrived with the init commit
describing coh-sidekick-1.0. The 25 entries and their reasons are recoverable from
`git show f3198ec73:scripts/dsh6-gate-allowlist.json` -- they are a useful record of gaps
that were closed, and the reasons distinguish 'by design' from 'known gap' carefully
enough to be worth reading before adding a new allowance.
What changed alongside this prune, and it is the half that matters: dsh6-collapse-
detector.cjs gained the REVERSE pass its two sibling gates already had, so an allowance
for a group that no longer occurs now prints 'stale allowance (group no longer occurs)'
on every run and the PASS line carries the counts. Without it this gate could only catch
a group that is NOT allowed -- never an allowance with nothing behind it -- which is how
a 100%-stale allowlist printed PASS for the life of the repository. A stale allowance is
how the next real drop gets waved through, so it has to be said out loud.
